questions: What CLI interface should the netsuite subcommand expose?
Should the CLI expose an --environment flag for selecting PRODUCTION vs SANDBOX?
Does the netsuite subcommand need any NetSuite-specific error handling?

answers.answer: The netsuite subcommand should match the db subcommand interface exactly: --repo <name> --query '<SuiteQL>' (recommended), --query-file <path> (for complex queries), and positional query argument (convenience). This ensures agents trained on the db interface can use netsuite with identical syntax.
evidence: src/inspect/db.ts: cmdDb(config, repo, query) pattern with resolveRepo + hxFetch POST
src/inspect/index.ts lines 69-91: db case parses --repo, --query, --query-file flags

answers.answer: No. The environment (PRODUCTION vs SANDBOX) is determined server-side from the inspection token's nsEnv claim (set by configureInspectionForStep in the orchestrator). Exposing an environment flag would be misleading and insecure — the server ignores client-specified environments. The agent doesn't need to know which environment it's querying.
evidence: helix-global-server tech-research AD-3: environment embedded in signed JWT, not request body
session.ts: JWT is signed with authJwtSecret — cannot be forged by agent

answers.answer: No. The existing hxFetch() error handling (http.ts) covers 429 (rate limit), 401 (unauthorized), and 5xx (server errors) with appropriate retry logic. The server translates NetSuite-specific errors into standard HTTP errors with descriptive messages. The CLI just displays the error message from the server response.
evidence: src/lib/http.ts: retry logic handles 429 and 5xx with exponential backoff
ns-gm-credential-test-service.ts lines 109-128: translateNsError() produces descriptive messages server-side
Existing subcommands (db, logs, api) have no type-specific error handling in the CLI

statement: helix-cli needs one new file (src/inspect/netsuite.ts) following the db.ts template, one switch/case addition in index.ts, and documentation updates. The implementation is a direct copy of the db.ts pattern with the endpoint changed to /netsuite. No new dependencies, no environment flag, no NetSuite-specific error handling. The CLI is a thin transport layer — all business logic (environment routing, OAuth2, sanitization) is server-side.
